title: Capitalize the Title
statement:
The string `title` is made of one or more words of English letters (any mix of upper and lower case), with exactly one space between neighbouring words. Rewrite the case of every word by this rule:

- a word of one or two letters becomes entirely lowercase;
- a word of three or more letters gets an uppercase first letter, and all its other letters become lowercase.

Return the resulting string; the words and spaces stay where they are.
constraints: title has no leading or trailing spaces, and words are separated by exactly one space
Each word is non-empty and contains only uppercase and lowercase English letters

tests.name: Test 10
input: to be or not to be

notes:
## Intuition

Every word is handled on its own, and the rule depends only on the word's length. So split `title` at the spaces, fix the case of each word, and glue the words back together with single spaces.

## Approach

1. Split `title` on spaces into `words`.
2. For each `word`, make it fully lowercase as `lower`.
3. If `lower` has at most 2 letters, keep it as is.
4. Otherwise uppercase its first letter and keep the rest lowercase.
5. Join `result` with single spaces and return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`"capiTalIze tHe titLe"` splits into `capiTalIze`, `tHe` and `titLe`. Lowercased they are `capitalize`, `the` and `title`; all have at least 3 letters, so each gets a capital first letter, and joining gives `"Capitalize The Title"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(L), where L is the length of `title`: every character is lowercased and copied a constant number of times.
- Space: O(L) for the words and the result.

## Pitfalls

- Lowercase the whole word first: letters after the first may be uppercase in the input.
- The threshold is "at most 2 letters stay lowercase"; a 3-letter word such as `the` is capitalized.
- Short words are lowercased even when they come first in the title.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `words` | the words of `title`, in order |
| `word` | the current word |
| `lower` | the current word in lowercase |
| `result` | the rewritten words, joined at the end |

narration.2: Cut the title into its words at the single spaces.
narration.5: Handle each word on its own.
narration.6: Start from the all-lowercase form; only the first letter may change after this.
narration.7: Words of one or two letters...
narration.10: Longer words get an uppercase first letter followed by the lowercase rest.
narration.13: Put the words back together with single spaces.
